subject.title: fix(doctor): bound legacy sessions.json reads during SQLite inspect

question: Should Doctor permanently treat otherwise valid legacy `sessions.json` stores above 16 MiB as unsupported, or must migration continue to preserve them?
rationale: This is a persistent-session upgrade-policy choice: the code can enforce either direction, but source evidence does not establish that a valid historical store may be excluded from migration.

options.title: Preserve migration for valid stores
options.body: Replace the hard support cutoff with a bounded/streaming migration design that still imports valid legacy data above 16 MiB.

options.title: Approve the 16 MiB retirement boundary
options.body: Explicitly accept that oversized valid legacy stores require operator intervention, with a documented data-preserving recovery path.

recommendation.title: Preserve migration for valid stores
recommendation.body: Replace the hard support cutoff with a bounded/streaming migration design that still imports valid legacy data above 16 MiB.

likelyOwner.reason: The author documented the proposed support boundary and can provide the migration-contract rationale, while current-main ownership history was not independently available.
